ops.title: Pre-12.22.4 updater reports success from brew's exit status, so an already-current Cellar logs 'update ok' while the host never moves — fixed upstream, still live on pinned installs
ops.description:
ALREADY FIXED UPSTREAM in 12.22.4 — this bug exists to record why a machine can still be running the broken version, and to close that gap.

THE DEFECT, as still installed on yasyf-box at ~/.local/share/uv/tools/capt-hook/lib/python3.13/site-packages/captain_hook/update/updater.py:118-120:

    if brew_upgrade():
        breadcrumb(f"update ok: {installed} -> {latest}")
        notify(kind="update_installed", title="Captain Hook updated", ...)

The outcome is read from brew's exit status. `brew install` exits 0 on an already-current Cellar, so this reports success unconditionally, including on every machine where 0ef22da2's sandbox denial silently blocked delivery. It also fires a "Captain Hook updated" desktop banner for an update that did not happen.

EVIDENCE — ~/.claude/state/update/update.log, three false successes while the host sat at 12.21.3 the entire time:

    2026-08-20T10:30:07.205541+00:00 update ok: 12.21.3 -> v12.21.6
    2026-08-30T01:09:11.746792+00:00 update ok: 12.21.3 -> v12.22.4
    2026-08-30T02:07:36.669676+00:00 update ok: 12.21.3 -> v12.22.4

Note the `v` prefix on the right-hand side: it is the release tag, never a version the host reported. The host was never asked.

THE UPSTREAM FIX, captain_hook/update/updater.py:88-105 in 12.22.4, gates on the host's own ping:

    def host_at_least(target: str) -> str | None:
        """... ``package-install`` supersedes the deployed app and returns only once the new
        host answers a ping, so the host's own reply is the proof that a brew lane landed
        rather than no-opped."""

and 12.22.4's module docstring already records the exact failure mode this bug describes ("one machine carried Cellar 12.21.6 for six days while its host stayed 12.21.4 and every check logged success"). The design is right.

WHY THE FIX DID NOT REACH THE MACHINE — this is the part worth acting on. The `capt-hook` CLI on PATH is not the Homebrew build. It is a uv tool pinned at 12.21.3:

    ~/.local/bin/capt-hook -> ~/.local/share/uv/tools/capt-hook/bin/capt-hook
    uv-receipt.toml: requirements = [{ name = "capt-hook", specifier = "==12.21.3" }]

Nothing upgrades it, and it is what `capt-hook update run` executes — so the component responsible for noticing that the host is stale was itself stale, and the one guaranteed to lie about it. `uv tool install --force 'capt-hook==12.22.4'` converges it.

Hook EXECUTION is unaffected: the host provisions its own version-matched interpreter at ~/.daemonkit/tools/capt-hook/12.22.4/capt-hook/bin/python, confirmed live in `capt-hookd status` after the 2026-08-29 converge. The blast radius is the interactive CLI and the updater lane, which is why this is P2 rather than P1.

A THIRD COPY IS ALSO STALE: ~/.claude/plugins/cache/captain-hook/captain-hook/12.21.6/. So on one machine the Homebrew formula (12.22.4), the uv CLI shim (12.21.3), and the Claude plugin cache (12.21.6) were three different versions simultaneously, with nothing reporting the split. That drift is the second acceptance criterion.

Filed alongside 0ef22da2 (the sandbox write-denial that this updater kept invisible) and 01ed7d3 (the HOME-resolution split that made the same failure silent).

ops.text: No installed capt-hook CLI in the fleet predates the host_at_least() gate; the uv-pinned 12.21.3 shim on yasyf-box is upgraded to 12.22.4
The CLI shim, the Claude plugin cache, and the Homebrew formula cannot drift into different major-minor versions without something reporting the split
